## **Understanding Medical Records Requests for Personal Injury Claims**


### **Why Complete Medical Documentation Determines Case Value**


Medical records are the foundation of every personal injury claim in Arlington. They link the incident to your client's injuries, document the extent of treatment, and provide the evidence needed for damages calculations. Without complete records from every treating provider, settlement talks stall and trial prep suffers.


The challenge is scale. A typical motor vehicle accident case involves emergency department records, diagnostic imaging, specialist consultations, physical therapy notes, and billing statements from multiple facilities. Each provider has its own authorization requirements, contact procedures, and response timelines.


### **The Impact of Timely Retrieval on Case Outcomes**


Texas deadlines depend on who holds the records and who's asking:


-


**Hospitals:** Under Health and Safety Code §241.154, hospitals generally must respond within 15 days after receiving the request and any applicable payment


-


**Physicians:** Physician practices generally have 15 business days, per the Texas Medical Board


-


**Patient electronic records:** Health and Safety Code §181.102 separately addresses qualifying patient requests for electronic records


-


**HIPAA patient access:** Generally 30 calendar days, with a limited extension permitted under specified conditions


Actual processing varies by provider, so separate processing time, delivery time, and legal deadlines when you plan a case. Incomplete or invalid authorizations can delay processing, so confirm when the custodian received a legally sufficient request and any permitted payment.


## **Essential Forms for Medical Record Release: Your HIPAA-Compliant Checklist**


### **Key Elements of a Valid HIPAA Authorization**


It helps to separate what[HIPAA requires](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.508) from what custodians ask for and what simply helps.


**Mandatory authorization elements:**


-


Specific description of the records requested


-


The provider or person authorized to disclose


-


The recipient (your firm)


-


Purpose of disclosure (legal purposes or personal injury claim)


-


An expiration date or expiration event. HIPAA doesn't require a specific window such as 60 to 180 days


-


Patient signature and date, plus a description of a representative's authority when one signs


-


Revocation rights statement


-


Statement about whether treatment, payment, enrollment, or benefits can be conditioned on signing


-


Redisclosure statement


**Custodian-specific identification requirements:**


-


Photo ID, handled according to each provider's instructions. Texas Health requests an ID copy with submissions, while USMD specifies identification at pickup


-


Any additional identifiers a custodian requests


**Recommended request details:**


-


Patient's full legal name, date of birth, and current address


-


Social Security number or account number when a common name needs disambiguating


-


Your firm's address, fax, and email for delivery


-


Clear date ranges


### **Authorization Forms by Provider Type**


**Texas Attorney General Standard Form**


The Texas Attorney General provides a[standard authorization form](https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/sites/default/files/files/divisions/consumer-protection/hb300-Authorization-Disclose-Health-Info.pdf) designed to support HIPAA and Texas compliance. Its instructions preserve other applicable legal requirements, so confirm it satisfies the custodian's requirements and any additional rules governing the records you need.


**Provider-Specific Forms**


Facility-specific forms can help avoid mismatches with a provider's requirements.[USMD Hospital Arlington](https://usmdarlington.com/patient-forms) offers a Patient Release Authorization form in English and Spanish.[Texas Health Resources](https://texashealth.org/Request-Medical-Records) publishes a General Authorization Form plus a separate Substance Abuse Authorization Form as part of its request procedure.[Medical City Arlington](https://medicalcityhealthcare.com/locations/medical-city-arlington-hospital) makes an Authorization for Release of Medical Information available through the MyHealthONE portal.[Baylor Scott & White](https://bswarlington.com/patients-visitors/medical-records) offers a Release of Information form for the Orthopedic and Spine Hospital.


### **Special Authorization Requirements**


Certain record types need extra attention beyond standard forms:


-


**Mental health records:** Psychotherapy notes have specific HIPAA protections and generally need their own authorization, separate from general mental health records


-


**Substance use treatment:** Records protected by[42 CFR Part 2](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-I/subchapter-A/part-2) require compliant consent or another lawful basis. The updated rule's compliance deadline was February 16, 2026, and separate restrictions apply to use in proceedings against a patient


-


**HIV/AIDS records:** Texas has additional state requirements


-


**Minor's records:** Parent or guardian authorization plus proof of guardianship


-


**Deceased patient records:** Establish the requester's authority under the applicable disclosure law and get the custodian's documentation requirements. For hospital records, Health and Safety Code §241.151 defines legally authorized representatives

## **Preventing Rejected Requests and Costly Delays**


### **Common Authorization Errors That Cause Delays**


Incomplete or invalid authorizations can stop a request from being processed. Common errors include:


-


Missing patient signature or signature date


-


Unclear or absent expiration date or event


-


Mishandled sections for sensitive record types (mental health, substance use, HIV)


-


Incorrect provider name or address


-


Date ranges that don't cover treatment periods


-


Forms missing elements that current law requires


### **Pre-Submission Validation Checklist**


Before sending any authorization, confirm that:


-


Patient name matches exactly as it appears in provider records


-


Date of birth is correct and clearly written


-


Provider name and address match the facility's legal name


-


Date range covers all relevant treatment periods


-


All required signature fields are completed


-


An expiration date or event is present


-


Sensitive record sections follow the form's instructions and any separate consent rules


-


Photo ID is handled the way the provider requires


-


The cover letter lists record types needed (ER, imaging, billing, complete chart)

**USMD Arlington:** Call (817) 472-2820 or email the HIM department directly.


**Baylor Scott & White:** Call the medical records numbers on its release form.


### **Suggested Internal Follow-Up Schedule**


These intervals are practice suggestions, not legal milestones. Base any escalation on the applicable deadline and request type.


**Days 1 to 3:** Look for confirmation of receipt. If none arrives, call HIM to verify.


**About day 7:** If the request is still pending, email the HIM supervisor with the patient name and submission date in the subject line.


**As the applicable deadline approaches:** Contact the HIM manager, ask for a written explanation of any delay, and cite the deadline that actually applies to your request.


**If records are needed for a trial or settlement deadline:** Consider a subpoena, depending on litigation posture and the applicable procedural and privacy requirements.


**For unresolved violations:** File a complaint with the[Texas Medical Board](https://www.tmb.texas.gov/file/citizen-complaint-process) for physicians, or with the HHS[Office for Civil Rights](https://www.hhs.gov/ocr/complaints/index.html) for appropriate HIPAA complaints.


### **Why Fast Isn't Always Complete**


Some vendors advertise same-day retrieval. According to Codes Health, services built around same-day turnaround often return only the records that are immediately available, not the complete set, which then requires client involvement to chase down the rest. Codes Health says that added back-and-forth frustrates clients and contributes to churn. Its approach aims for complete records in weeks, not months.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How long do Arlington facilities retain medical records after treatment ends?**


It depends on the provider type. Under Health and Safety Code §241.103, hospitals must keep records for 10 years after the last treatment, or for patients last treated as minors, until age 20 or 10 years after last treatment, whichever is later. Hospitals also can't destroy relevant records while they know litigation remains unresolved. Physician practices generally keep records at least seven years after the last treatment, with additional rules for minors, per the Texas Medical Board. Submit requests promptly for older treatment dates.


### **Can I request radiology images (X-rays, CT scans, MRI) along with written reports?**


Yes, but imaging requests often need separate handling. Medical City Arlington directs imaging requests to its Radiology Department rather than standard HIM channels. Ask each facility for a written quote covering images and delivery, and specify whether you need written reports only or actual diagnostic images. For litigation requiring expert review, request both the radiologist's report and the original DICOM files.


### **What happens if a provider claims they have no records for my client?**


First, verify the patient information matches exactly, including name spelling, date of birth, and dates of service. Common names may need extra identifiers like Social Security or account numbers. If the provider still has no records, ask for written confirmation of the search performed and date ranges checked. That protects your file if records surface later. For clients with incomplete recollection of where they were treated, Codes Health uses provider and facility data to help identify where records may exist.


### **Are there additional fees for certified copies or records affidavits for trial?**


Often, yes. Get a written quote for certification, affidavits, and delivery, since charges vary and a statutory maximum isn't the same as a provider's actual charge. USMD, for example, references applicable legal limits for certification. If you'll need certified records for trial, say so in your initial request, as some facilities require a separate request for certification.


### **How do I handle records requests for facilities that have closed or merged?**


Closures and mergers complicate access. Texas has no centralized state repository for these records, so locate the designated custodian or successor organization. For physician practices, check the[Texas Medical Board's custodian](https://www.tmb.texas.gov/resources/for-the-public/patient-information-and-medical-records) information. For merged facilities, start with the current organization's HIM department, which often retains access to predecessor records. Texas Health Resources, for example, processes requests for care across its hospitals through its central office.
